# Stocks jump as oil tumbles, Nvidia falls amid internal probe

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Dhara Ranasinghe

November 9, 2026 1:46 AM UTC Updated ago

- Major US stock indexes gain more than 2% each
- Oil drops as Trump downplays risk of new Iran strikes
- Nvidia shares fall sharply amid internal investigation

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Major stock indexes rallied on Monday as Brent crude oil fell more than 5% after ​US President Donald Trump said he is unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran, while shares of Nvidia (NVDA.O), opens new tab dropped.

The fall in ‌oil prices helped to ease worries about inflation that have weighed on economies across the globe this year.

Trump on Sunday said that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the war progressed, even though both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude ​futures fell $5.75, or 5.85%, to settle at $92.57 a barrel, and prices continued falling after settlement, while US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped $3.98, ​or 4.38%, to $86.85.

Efforts to end the Iran war have gathered pace following last week's US midterm elections in which Democrats won ⁠control of Congress.

Shares of Nvidia, the second-most valuable company in the world, tumbled 4.2% and closed at their lowest level since April 7, with investors ​questioning CEO Jensen Huang's future at the AI chipmaker after an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him.

However, the three major US stock ​indexes finished more than 2% higher, with the S&P 500 (.SPX), opens new tab rebounding from its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. Last week's selloff was tied to the US midterm elections and worries about increased AI and data center regulation.

"We have seen a very steep and exaggerated selloff in the market," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in ​New York. "Whenever the market gets that stretched to the downside, history has shown us usually it's a good buying opportunity in the short term."

The buying ​comes from "shorts that have to cover" positions, value investors looking for bargains and from momentum traders, Sarhan said.

An index of semiconductors (.SOX), opens new tab surged 6.9% after plunging more than 12% ‌last week. ⁠Nvidia was the only decliner in the index on Monday.

Europe remains in driver's seat


Published:
5 November, 2026

### Highlights

- Global gold ETFs continued to expand, adding US$2.7bn in October, led by European funds.
- Global gold ETF holdings rose 19t to 4,275t, but their AUM fell 6% to US$542bn due to the lower gold price in the month.
- Global gold market trading volumes pulled back, due mainly to cooling activity in exchange-traded derivatives.

### October in review

**Global physically-backed gold ETFs** [**1**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-1) **attracted US$2.7bn in October, having expanded for four consecutive months (Chart 1).** Notably, European funds led the charge with sizable inflows. Asian investors remained net buyers while North America saw marginal outflows. Global gold ETFs’ collective holdings climbed 19t to 4,275t, another month-end record. Meanwhile, assets under management (AUM) fell 6% to US$542bn as the lower gold price overshadowed inflows.

During the first ten months of the year, global gold ETFs added US$41bn, the third strongest on record, and their holdings rose by 246t. European and Asian investors led global flows, each accounting for 44% and 45% of total net inflows, respectively. At the country level, the UK recorded the largest inflows, with China a close second.

**Chart 1: European inflows continued to lead despite the price pull back**

Global gold ETF flows by region and the monthly average gold price\*

![](https://www.gold.org/sites/default/files/inline-images/image_36.png)

\*As of 31 October 2026. Gold price based on the quarterly and monthly average LBMA Gold Price PM in USD.

Source: Bloomberg, Company Filings, World Gold Council

### Regional overview

**North American funds saw modest outflows of US$512mn, the only region with outflows in October.** US-domiciled gold ETFs were the sole driver of the region’s October loss; Canadian funds continued to attract inflows.

US technology equities came under selling pressure during October amid growing concerns around AI-related capital spend. The resulting market stress may have contributed to the region’s gold ETF outflows as some investors turned to their gold holdings as a ready source of liquidity. This illustrates one of gold’s key attributes: deep liquidity can help investors meet cash needs during market turbulence.

Equity sell-offs in the month also led to strong safe-haven buying of US Treasuries. October saw their strongest monthly return since December 2023 and pulled yields down from the highest in nearly 25 years. [2](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-2) Relatively attractive price levels and investor repricing of a less aggressive US Fed may have increased their appeal. This focus on US Treasuries could have diverted investors away from gold.

Yet it is worth noting that US gold ETFs saw net inflows, albeit mild, during the last week of October when local equities plunged again. This reflects investors’ strategic allocation, possibly driven by a combination of diversification needs against political uncertainty – with midterm elections around the corner – and persisting fiscal concerns.

**Europe has now seen inflows for four months in a row, adding US$1.8bn in October.** The UK continued to lead, with funds listed in Germany, Switzerland and France also registering positive demand.

It is worth highlighting that the region has experienced net inflows for 18 consecutive weeks. This is a trend that has persisted despite the gold price weakness, surging yields across the region, and changes in market expectations of future moves by local central banks.

This suggests that demand for gold ETFs may be increasingly strategic, reflecting persistent political and fiscal uncertainty across the region. In France, social unrest, political fragmentation and a difficult fiscal consolidation have weighed on investor sentiment, unsettling domestic equities and adding to sovereign risk premia. [3](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-3) In the UK, elevated yields, energy shocks and shrinking fiscal headroom also sparked concerns. [4](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-4) Meanwhile, Germany is experiencing weakening economic momentum and growing political pressure on its governing coalition. Against this backdrop, investors have increasingly turned to gold ETFs for diversification, particularly as traditional safe-haven bond markets face their own challenges.

**Asian investors bought US$1.3bn in October, also a fourth consecutive month of inflows.** China continued to lead the region’s inflows. Local investor allocation to gold ETFs remains strategically linked to the equity market rout and falling government bond yields, which reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold despite the gold price weakness. Japanese gold ETFs continued to attract inflows in October, driven by similar factors: the Nikkei pulled back and Japanese government bond yields fell amid safe-haven flows and less aggressive expectations of the BoJ’s tightening ahead for most of the month – the central bank left rates unchanged in late October. [5](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-5) India also saw sustained gold ETF buying in the month despite local mutual funds’ [temporary suspension of fresh subscription to gold fund of funds](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q3-2026/investment) in mid-October.

**Gold ETFs listed in other regions saw mild inflows of US$62mn**, supported throughout the month by demand from both Australia and South Africa.

**Chart 2: UK and China lead global inflows y-t-d**

Cumulative ETF fund flows by selected countries\*

![UK and China lead global inflows y-t-d](https://www.gold.org/sites/default/files/inline-images/chart-2.png)

\*As of 31 October 2026. Countries shown are the five largest contributors to global gold ETF inflows y-t-d.

Source: Bloomberg, Company Filings, World Gold Council

## Gold ETF flows

Data as of 6 November, 2026

Demand captures changes in global/regional gold holdings; fund flows capture the net amount of money (in USD) that comes in or out of gold ETFs globally/regionally. See [methodology note](https://www.gold.org/download/file/16223/ETF-Flows-Data-Methodology.pdf).

### Volumes eased

[**Global gold market volumes**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-trading-volumes) [**6**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-6) **declined 13% in October, averaging US$365bn per day.** All sectors saw volumes pull back. Over-the-counter (OTC) volumes decreased by a marginal 2%, to US$219bn/day – LBMA activities remained healthy at US$196bn/day, with only a 2% m/m decline and well above the 2025 average of US$161bn/day. Exchange-traded activity fell the most, shedding 25% in the month to US$140bn/day, led by a 22% decline at the COMEX and a 31% retreat in Shanghai. Liquidity of global gold ETFs averaged US$6bn/day in the month, a 20% m/m fall, primarily driven by North America which accounted for the lion’s share of total.

[**Total COMEX net longs**](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-open-interest) **fell further, shedding 94t in October to 560t, the lowest since end-July.** [7](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-7) Net longs held by managed money reduced 53t in the month. Meanwhile, other reportables [8](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-8) continued to retreat, losing 54t, and spreads [9](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-9) pulled back by 13t. Interestingly, net open interest [10](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-etfs-holdings-and-flows/2026/11#footnote-10) of COMEX gold options rose 6% in the month, and kept climbing during the last few days of October despite the equity sell-off, possibly due to rollovers amid contract expiry and potential dip buying.

**Chart 3: Gold market trading volumes fell in October**

Average daily trading volumes by segment\*

![](https://www.gold.org/sites/default/files/inline-images/image_38.png)

\*Data as of 31 October 2026. Gold price based on the monthly average LBMA Gold Price PM USD.

For more information on trading volumes please visit our Trading Volumes page on Goldhub: [Gold Trading Volume \| Gold Daily Volume \| World Gold Council.](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/gold-trading-volumes)

Source: Bloomberg, Nasdaq, COMEX, ICE Benchmark Administration, Shanghai Gold Exchange, Shanghai Futures Exchange, ETF providers, Multi Commodity Exchange of India, Dubai Gold & Commodities Exchange, Japan Exchange Group, Thailand Futures Exchange, Borsa Istanbul, Bursa Malaysia, Korea Exchange, World Gold Council

### Footnotes

01. We define gold ETFs as regulated securities that hold gold in physical form. These include open-ended funds traded on regulated exchanges and other regulated products such as closed-end funds and mutual funds. A complete list is included in the gold ETF section of [Goldhub.com](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/).

02. Based on Bloomberg US Agg Total Return Index and the US 10-year Treasury yield. On 7 October 2026, the 10-year yield surged to the highest since 4 April 2002.

03. See: [French student protests pause, pressure builds amid budget deadlock](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/07/french-student-protests-budget-deadlock.html), 7 October 2026.

04. See: [UK fiscal headroom narrows to £11bn says EY analysis \| EY - UK](https://www.ey.com/en_uk/newsroom/2026/10/uk-fiscal-headroom-could-fall-to-7bn-deficit), 5 October 2026.

05. See: [Monetary Policy Meetings : 日本銀行 Bank of Japan](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

06. Due to LBMA trading volume data availability our full trading volume dataset dates back to 2019.

07. Based on CFTC positioning report as of 28 October 2026.

08. Other reportables refer to reportable traders in the CFTC Commitment of Traders report that do not fall into the producer/merchant, swap dealer, or managed money categories. This group can include institutional or commercial participants with positions large enough to meet reporting thresholds.

09. Spreading positions reflect investors with offsetting long and short positions, typically in different calendar months.

10. Net option open interest (OI) measures the difference between outstanding call and put option contracts, providing a broad indication of options-market sentiment rather than a direct measure of directional exposure.

# Crypto Market Today, Nov. 9: Bitcoin and Ethereum Lag as Nasdaq Surges Nearly 3%

![](https://media.zenfs.com/en/motleyfool.com/5dc1e0171807c5f39ae2901c0370f05c.jpg)

Cryptocurrencies struggled to gain momentum on Monday despite a sharp recovery across Wall Street. As of early evening on November 9, **Bitcoin** (CRYPTO:BTC) edged up 0.14% to $74,824.47, while **Ethereum** (CRYPTO:ETH) gained 0.11% to $2,126.59. **Solana** (CRYPTO:SOL) rose 0.19% to $86.48. The muted performance stood in sharp contrast to the Nasdaq Composite's nearly 3% rally, underscoring continued weakness across digital assets.

## What's driving crypto markets

Cryptocurrency markets continued to struggle on Monday, even as investors returned to technology and semiconductor stocks following last week's sharp sell-off. While the broader equity market staged a strong recovery, Bitcoin remained below $75,000, suggesting that selling pressure across digital assets has yet to subside.

Institutional demand remains a major concern. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, their largest weekly withdrawal since late June. Ethereum ETFs experienced another $365 million in outflows, bringing combined withdrawals to roughly $1.65 billion.

Meanwhile, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin recently weighed in on the cryptocurrency's long-term investment case, arguing that its value should be rooted more in security, decentralization, and stability than in transaction fee burns. While the comments highlight Ethereum's evolving positioning, investors remain focused on deteriorating market momentum and the broader macroeconomic outlook.

## Crypto ETF snapshot

Spot cryptocurrency ETFs also traded lower on Monday. The **iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF** (NASDAQ:IBIT) declined 1.31%, while the **Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund** (NYSEMKT:FBTC) fell 1.34%. The **iShares Ethereum Trust ETF** (NASDAQ:ETHA) dropped 4.51%, reflecting continued pressure across cryptocurrency-linked investments despite the broader stock market recovery.

## What this means for investors

Monday's divergence between [cryptocurrencies](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/types-of-cryptocurrencies/?utm_source=yahoo-host-full&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=bbd6a90c-43d9-4136-b255-e0b2ab0f3ec5) and technology stocks is not what investors hoping for a sustained recovery want to see. Bitcoin's ability to defend the $74,000 to $75,000 region is becoming increasingly important. A sustained break below this range could expose the market to further losses, while a recovery above $80,000 would offer a more encouraging sign that buyers are returning. Ethereum and Solana face similar challenges, having surrendered much of their earlier gains and now trading near important support levels.

Perhaps the clearest signal to watch is institutional demand. After more than $1 billion in Bitcoin ETF outflows last week, a sustained return to positive flows would help establish whether investors are regaining confidence. Equally important will be whether cryptocurrencies begin to outperform technology stocks rather than continue to lag during broader market rallies.

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Major stock indexes rallied on Monday as Brent crude oil fell more than 5% after ​US President  Donald Trump  said he is unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran, while shares of Nvidia  (NVDA.O)     , opens new tab   dropped.
The fall in ‌oil prices helped to ease worries about inflation that have weighed on economies across the globe this year.
 Trump on Sunday  said that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the war progressed, even though both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.  Brent crude  ​futures fell $5.75, or 5.85%, to settle at $92.57 a barrel, and prices continued falling after settlement, while US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped $3.98, ​or 4.38%, to $86.85.
Efforts to end the  Iran war  have gathered pace following last week's  US midterm elections  in which Democrats won ⁠control of Congress.
Shares of  Nvidia , the second-most valuable company in the world, tumbled 4.2% and closed at their lowest level since April 7, with investors ​questioning CEO Jensen Huang's future at the AI chipmaker after an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him.
However, the  three major US stock ​indexes  finished more than 2% higher, with the S&P 500  (.SPX)     , opens new tab   rebounding from its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. Last week's selloff was tied to the US midterm elections and worries about increased AI and data center regulation.
"We have seen a very steep and exaggerated selloff in the market," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in ​New York. "Whenever the market gets that stretched to the downside, history has shown us usually it's a good buying opportunity in the short term."
The buying ​comes from "shorts that have to cover" positions, value investors looking for bargains and from momentum traders, Sarhan said.
An index of semiconductors  (.SOX)     , opens new tab   surged 6.9% after plunging more than 12% ‌last week. ⁠Nvidia was the only decliner in the index on Monday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average  (.DJI)     , opens new tab   rose 1,104.02 points, or 2.15%, to 52,389.75, the S&P 500  (.SPX)     , opens new tab   rose 173.08 points, or 2.35%, to 7,549.94 and the Nasdaq Composite  (.IXIC)     , opens new tab   rose 673.71 points, or 2.74%, to 25,253.14.
Earnings reports due this week from tech companies including CoreWeave  (CRWV.O)     , opens new tab  , Applied Materials  (AMAT.O)     , opens new tab   and Cisco Systems  (CSCO.O)     , opens new tab   are set to put the profitability of AI ambitions to the test amid the massive costs of the buildout.
CoreWeave has become ​a barometer of  investor anxiety over AI     , opens new tab  , ​and the cost of insuring its ⁠debt has spiked into distressed territory recently.
US Treasury yields rose ahead of the US ​October consumer price report ⁠on Tuesday, which may sway whether the Federal Reserve hikes interest rates at its December meeting.
Economists polled by Reuters expect headline consumer inflation to have risen 0.3% last month, with core posting a 0.2% increase.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 1.48 basis points to 4.874%.
Bets for a December Fed rate hike rose ⁠after Friday's  blowout ​jobs report  showed US employers added 165,000 jobs last month. Fed funds futures traders now see ​an 84% chance of a hike next month.
The dollar eased, with the euro up 0.72% at $1.1223. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.34% to 157.91.

Nov 9 (Reuters) - Gold prices ​climbed more than 1% on Monday as the dollar eased and inflationary jitters ‌took a back seat due to lower crude oil prices, while markets awaited US inflation data later this week.
Spot gold was up 1% at $4,107.01 per ounce by 1:35 p.m. ET (1830 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery ​settled 1% higher at $4,114.50.
"We're seeing a lower US dollar index on this first day ​of the trading week," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American ⁠Gold Exchange.
"We're seeing lower crude oil prices today that suggest receding inflationary fears — that's positive ​for the gold and silver markets, on ideas that lessening inflation fears will allow the central ​banks to lean easier on their monetary policies."
The US dollar eased, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for overseas buyers.
Oil dropped sharply after  US President Donald Trump  downplayed the likelihood of renewed strikes on  Iran , though attacks on ships near ​the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus.
Higher energy prices have fed inflation fears ​since the onset of the US-Israeli war on Iran in late February. Stronger inflation forces central banks to ‌adopt a ⁠higher-for-longer interest rate stance to keep cost pressures in check.
Although gold is a traditional safe-haven asset, it loses its appeal to yield-bearing assets in a high interest rate environment.
Bullion gained around 5% last week as Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm ​elections, a result that ​raised hopes for an ⁠end to the war with Iran.
However, prices eased after stronger-than-expected US payrolls data on Friday reinforced expectations that the Fed could keep rates higher ​for longer.
Traders currently see an 82.2% chance of a December rate ​hike, the  CME's FedWatch ⁠tool     , opens new tab   showed.
The market is awaiting US consumer price data on Tuesday and producer price figures on Friday, which could give more clues on the Fed's trajectory for rates.
Elsewhere, China's central bank added about 25.8 ⁠metric ​tons of gold to its reserves in October, the largest ​monthly purchase in three years, according to World Gold Council data.
Spot silver climbed 1.8% to $52.78, platinum gained 1.8% to $1,561.00, and ​palladium rose 0.3% to $1,026.26.

# Banks that raced to fund neoclouds like CoreWeave are now hesitating
CEO Michael Intrator called borrowing against those chips “a very cost effective way to access the debt markets.”
That approach became a template for neoclouds, the companies that rent AI computing power to tech firms.
...
## Lenders now want to know who can walk away
Lenders are also scrutinizing contract details, Reuters noted, including:
- **Service obligations** spell out what a neocloud must deliver.
- **Operational deadlines** set when new capacity must go live.
- **Exit conditions** define when a large tech customer can reduce or end its commitment.
That last point may matter most, because neoclouds borrow against customer contracts.
CoreWeave reported a revenue backlog of about **$104 billion** at the end of June, according to its second-quarter earnings release.
A backlog protects a lender only if the customer cannot easily leave.
Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) accounted for about 67% of CoreWeave’s 2025 revenue, according to its annual report.
Microsoft plans to use fewer neocloud partners, CNBC reported.
Intrator wrote on LinkedIn that he does not currently expect political shifts to affect CoreWeave’s existing commitments or backlog, CNBC reported.

# Microsoft Borrows at “10 Percentage Points Below CoreWeave.” Now It’s Backing Away From Neoclouds
...

...
- Microsoft wants fewer neocloud partners and won't renew one of its cloud contracts with Oracle, CNBC reported on Friday.
- Citi's Steven Wieting says Microsoft's cost of debt is about 10 percentage points below CoreWeave's.
That makes owning data centers much cheaper for Microsoft than renting them.
...
- CoreWeave has the most to lose, and its results in the coming days will show how much it depends on Microsoft.
**Microsoft (** **MSFT:NASDAQ** **)** helped create the neocloud boom.
Now it's backing away from it, and **CoreWeave (** **CRWV:NASDAQ** **)** and **Oracle (** **ORCL:NYSE** **)** stand to lose business.
On Friday, CNBC's Seema Modi reported on Closing Bell Overtime that Microsoft has decided not to renew one of its cloud contracts with Oracle.
Her sources also said Microsoft "is actively looking at shrinking the number of neoclouds it partners with as it doubles down on its own data center strategy."
On the same show, Citi's Steven Wieting put a number on Microsoft's edge.
Its cost of debt, he said, "is about 10 percentage points below CoreWeave."
That's an enormous head start.
...
In the September quarter, it was the only one of the five biggest AI spenders with positive free cash flow.
At June 30, it held $76.8 billion of cash and short-term investments against $40.3 billion of debt.
...
CoreWeave is in a very different spot, since it borrows to build.
Its total debt climbed from $6.28 billion at the end of September 2024 to $51.6 billion at the end of June 2026:
CoreWeave (CRWV): total debt, $ billions, last 8 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)
And it's paying more to borrow.
Steve Eisman, of The Big Short fame, said on The Real Eisman Playbook that CoreWeave's debt was repriced weeks ago from a yield of 9% to 15%.
"At a cost of debt of 15%, building AI data centers becomes prohibitively expensive," he said.
...
Losing Microsoft work would hurt CoreWeave twice.
Modi noted on CNBC that the publicly listed neoclouds use Microsoft's AAA credit rating to secure loans.
So fewer Microsoft contracts could mean less revenue and also costlier borrowing, for a company that already owes a lot.
The pullback has been building, too: Microsoft rejected Nscale's Texas expansion on Thursday, and CoreWeave sank 9%.
Oracle's hit is smaller: one contract, tied to older A100 chips.
...
The catch for Microsoft is speed.
It has been adding about 1 gigawatt of capacity a quarter, and management has said demand still exceeds what it has.
Any in-house build that comes online later than a neocloud's would have costs Azure sales.
Ford also pointed out that demand is strong enough for a company like Meta or Google to take capacity Microsoft passes up, and that's CoreWeave's best case.
...
Of course, CoreWeave's results in the coming days should show how much of its business still comes from Microsoft, and whether other buyers are filling the gap.

## Quarterly Refunding Statement of Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets Hunter McMaster

November 4, 2026

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury is offering $125 billion of Treasury securities to refund approximately $97 billion of privately-held Treasury notes and bonds maturing on November 15, 2026. This issuance will raise new cash from private investors of approximately $28 billion. The securities are:

- A 3-year note in the amount of $58 billion, maturing November 15, 2029;
- A 10-year note in the amount of $42 billion, maturing November 15, 2036;
- A 30-year bond in the amount of $25 billion, maturing November 15, 2056.

The 3-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Monday, November 9, 2026. The 10-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The 30-year bond will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Thursday, November 12, 2026. All these auctions will take place on a yield basis and will settle on Monday, November 16, 2026. 

The balance of Treasury financing requirements over the quarter will be met with regular weekly bill auctions, cash management bills (CMBs), and monthly note, bond, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS), and 2-year Floating Rate Note (FRN) auctions.

### NOMINAL COUPON AND FRN FINANCING

Treasury believes its current auction sizes leave it well positioned to address potential changes to the fiscal outlook and to the size and composition of the SOMA portfolio. Based on current projected borrowing needs, Treasury anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the next several quarters. Treasury is monitoring SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing demand for Treasury bills from the private sector. Looking ahead, Treasury continues to evaluate potential future changes to nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes, with a focus on trends in structural demand and potential costs and risks of various issuance profiles. As part of that process, Treasury will engage with a variety of market participants to better understand evolving Treasury supply and demand dynamics. In considering any changes, Treasury will be guided by the objective of financing the government at the lowest cost over time.
